newsitem.title: GHANA: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --
GHANA, October 21 to November 4 - Tema, Takoradi - No berthing delays expected.

ISRAEL, October 29 - Haifa - Four vessels due, 1-2 days delay expected. Delays for loading/discharging at berth, general cargo up to 1 day, bulk up to 3 days, containers 5 days, tankers 2 days. Delays for vessels waiting at anchorage to load/discharge, general cargo up to 1 day, bulk up to 3 days. 4 Vessels under repair/drydock, 3 awaiting orders. Ashdod - Delays for loading/discharging at berth, general cargo up to 9 days, bulk 1-2 days, containers 3 days, car carriers, tankers 1 day. Delays waiting at anchorage to load/discharge, general cargo 1 day, bulk up to 2 days, containers 2 days. Eilat - Delays for vessels loading/discharging at berth, tankers 1 day.

MOZAMBIQUE, October 28 - Nacala - Port working normally (first come, first served basis). No restriction on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restriction of 9.5 metres plus height of tide at general cargo berths and 14 metres at container berths. One tugboat available. Beira - General cargo berths working normally (first come, first served basis). Container terminal/other terminals working normally. Pilotage is now possible 24 hours a day for vessels up to 140 metres loa with a maximum draft of 7.5 metres. Two tugboats now fully operational. Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangements with the port captain. Maputo - Pilotage is now possible 24 hours a day for vessels up to 120 metres loa with a maximum draft of 9 metres. Two tugboats available, one out of order. Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangements with the port captain. All berths working normally and expected to remain so (first come, first served basis). Draft restriction in the channel is 9 metres less 0.5 metre plus rise of tide.
NAMIBIA, October 28 - Walvis Bay - Working normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, October 28 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths, fully committed with berthing delays of between 24 to 48 hours. Bulk import berths, fully committed. Bulk export berths (minerals, etc.), no. 3 belt under repairs until 31/10. Bulk export berths, 2 vessels anchorage awaiting berthing turn, 10 due by 3/11, no congestion expected. Berthing on arrival for remainder of the week. Durban - Container terminal, delays of up to 48 hours currently. Point/New Pier/Maydon Wharf berths, working normally for general cargo vessels, but delays for wheat dischargers can be expected. Maize terminal (Maydon Wharf 8), 2 maize loaders for November. Citrus terminal, last vessel on 31/10 for season.

Bunker supplies, delays in supplying of bunkers can be expected due to bunching of vessels. Drydock and floating dock, 85 percent booked for November. East London - General cargo/combi terminal berths busy but no delays. Drydock, booked for November and up to 27 December. Copper moving in small parcels per month in containers to Far East. Elevator, 1 vessel due mid-November. Gas oil pipeline under-utilised. Wheat imports, 1 vessel discharging in port. Tankers, expect to be busy for next 2 months. Port Elizabeth - Six vessels in port, no delays on general, ore or tanker berths. Container berth, 2 vessels in port, 2 due on 28/10 with delays of 12 hours for one. Cape Town - Breakbulk berths, no delays, vessels working on arrival. Container terminal, no delays expected, but strong winds may be a factor. Bunker berths, no delays expected. Drydock fully occupied, booking essential. Saldanha Bay - Working normally.

TUNISIA, October 26 - Gabes - Three vessels loading at berth (stpp in bags, bulk fertiliser, container vessel), 2 bulk fertiliser waiting at anchor to load. Sfax - Seven vessels operating of which 2 discharging steel, 1 discharging bulk sulphur, 1 loading bulk salt, 1 loading bulk tsp, 1 loading bulk rock phosphate, 1 passenger vessel. Tunis - Four vessels in port of which awaiting instructions, 1 general cargo, 1 discharging marble blocks, 1 other vessel. Rades - Three ro/ro vessels in port. Goulette, north side - 1 Passenger vessel, 1 military vessel, 1 cereal vessel in port. South side - 1 Vessel discharging grain. Two vessels in roads. Sousse - Two military vessels in port, no waiting time, no vessels awaiting orders.

YEMEN, October 28 - Hodeidah - Three vessels alongside of which 2 wheat, 1 wheat flour, none anchored. Delays general cargo up to 2 days, bagged cargo 4 days, bulk cargo 6 days, containers 1 day. Mokha - One discharging wheatflour, none anchored/waiting. Hodeidah - Berthed 2 bulk wheat, 1 flour. 1 Paper rolls vessel awaiting berth. Delays bagged cargo 24 days, no other delays.
